clinical_knowledge.topic: Carpal Tunnel Syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Carpal Tunnel right wrist: Nocturnal neutral wrist splint, schedule EMG/NCS, ergonomics, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Carpal Tunnel Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Cervical radiculopathy (C6/C7) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Thenar muscle atrophy.

boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with chief complaint of burning pain and hand numbness, Phalen test positive. HPI: carpal tunnel syndrome.
reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Carpal Tunnel right wrist.
reference_soap.assessment: Condition highly suspicious for Carpal Tunnel right wrist.
reference_soap.plan: For suspected right carpal tunnel syndrome, trial a nocturnal neutral wrist splint and ergonomic modification. Consider EMG/NCS for persistent, atypical, or motor symptoms; arrange prompt specialist assessment for thenar weakness or atrophy. Counsel the patient.

teaching.one_liner: Entrapment of the median nerve within the carpal tunnel causing nocturnal numbness and tingling in the radial three and a half digits.

must_ask.say: Are the numbness and burning located in your thumb, index, and middle fingers?
Does the hand numbness wake you up at night needing to shake your hands for relief?
Do you drop objects frequently or struggle to open jars or button shirts?
Do you perform repetitive wrist flexing activities or heavy computer typing?
Does holding your wrists bent together worsen the tingling within a minute?
